By Science Correspondent

Stickleback fish can change the way they behave in groups to help them find food when the water around them becomes cloudy, a University of Bristol study has found.

Researchers from the university’s School of Biological Sciences looked at shoals of three-spined sticklebacks and how they responded when the water became increasingly murky.


They also watched how quickly the fish reacted when food was suddenly introduced.
